title: Emrys and the Inheritance
premise: True-crime podcaster Jonah Amberdale has spent a decade documenting the unsolved disappearance of schoolteacher Vera Loxley, the coldest case in the river town of Hallowmere. When a drowned body surfaces wearing clothes stolen from Jonah's own closet, police name him a suspect — and he realizes someone is staging his podcast's theories back at him as evidence. To clear his name, Jonah must reopen what the town swore was closed: proving that Vera was murdered by the respected family whose inheritance depended on her silence. In the end, Jonah exposes the killer using the dead woman's own hidden recordings, trading his career and the town's comfortable lies for a justice the law can no longer deliver.
about_author: Emrys Ravensworth spent seven years as a small-town court reporter before turning to fiction, a career that left him fluent in the gap between what courts decide and what actually happened. He lives near a slow brown river and insists the best mysteries are filed under 'accident.'

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Introduces his obsessive archive of the Vera Loxley case and the tenth anniversary episode of his podcast. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness; Jonah has organized grief into a filing system to avoid feeling it.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A corpse pulled from the millrace wears Jonah's own missing coat and scarf. Detective Ilsa Vann treats him as suspect first, fan second. Emotional beat: violation — his private obsession made public and weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Rain
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter from Vera's POV, ten years earlier: her last week alive, her growing fear of the Ashcombe family she tutored. Emotional beat: dread building toward warmth; readers meet Vera as a person, not a case file.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe House Rules
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He interviews patriarch Edmund Ashcombe, who inherited everything when Vera vanished, and notices a portrait turned to face the wall. Emotional beat: polite menace; wealth as an alibi.

chapters.title: Suspect Number One
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vann's POV. The detective builds her case against Jonah while privately doubting it; the staged clothing is too theatrical for him. Emotional beat: professional suspicion curdling into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Letters Never Sent
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Among Vera's effects he finds unmailed letters hinting she discovered something about the Ashcombe inheritance — a will, a death, a lie. Emotional beat: hope rekindled, then guilt for hoping.

chapters.title: The Podcast Eats Its Host
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Listeners turn on him; sponsors flee; an anonymous account posts episode transcripts annotated with corrections only the killer could know. Emotional beat: public unraveling; his archive becomes a noose.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Vera's POV flashback. She records a cassette tape detailing what she saw in the Ashcombe house and hides it, telling no one. Emotional beat: quiet courage; a witness choosing to testify even if no one ever listens.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He traces the money: Vera's disappearance conveniently voided a codicil that would have exposed old Edmund's brother's fraud. Emotional beat: cold clarity — the motive was never passion, it was paperwork.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. A retired clerk who once handled the Ashcombe estate papers dies of 'natural causes' days after Jonah contacts him. Emotional beat: horror; the case is not cold, it is actively defended.

chapters.title: House of Turned Portraits
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He breaks into the shuttered east wing of Ashcombe House and finds Vera's handwriting penciled inside a wardrobe — the same closet his stolen clothes came from. Emotional beat: vertigo; past and present folding into one room.

chapters.title: Confessions on Tape
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Jonah finds half of Vera's cassette in the parish archive; Ilsa finds the other half referenced in the clerk's shredded files. They compare notes off the record. Emotional beat: wary alliance between accuser and investigator.

chapters.title: The Town That Swore
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating brief POVs: shopkeeper, priest, retired teacher — each recalling how the town agreed to call Vera's death an accident. Emotional beat: collective complicity; silence as a civic project.

chapters.title: Edmund's Last Will
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Dying Edmund summons Jonah and offers him money and the truth in exchange for burying the tape. Jonah refuses. Emotional beat: temptation and its refusal; the moment Jonah stops being a documentarian and becomes a participant.

chapters.title: Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: POV of Marcus Ashcombe, Edmund's son, who has been staging the copycat evidence to frame Jonah and protect the inheritance. Emotional beat: chilling intimacy inside the antagonist's rational mind.

chapters.title: The Trap Closes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Marcus plants forged tapes implicating Jonah directly; Ilsa must arrest the man she has come to believe is innocent. Emotional beat: despair at the machinery of procedure outpacing the truth.

chapters.title: Night at the Millrace
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fleeing arrest, Jonah returns to the millrace where Vera died and reconstructs her final hour from tide marks, weather logs, and memory. Emotional beat: communion with the dead; fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Vera Speaks
chapters.summary: Vera's POV, final flashback interwoven with present tense: her full recording plays as Jonah broadcasts it live, unedited, naming names. Emotional beat: catharsis; ten years of silence broken in nineteen minutes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Proof
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Confronted with the broadcast and corroborating estate documents, Ilsa arrests Marcus — knowing the statute has run out on the original crime. Emotional beat: bitter triumph; justice arrives wearing handcuffs it cannot legally close.

chapters.title: What the Law Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Marcus, untouchable for Vera's murder but nailed for the clerk's, faces the town at trial; Jonah testifies not as expert but as neighbor. Emotional beat: reckoning; the community forced to hear its own silence read aloud.

chapters.title: The Empty Closet
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. He dismantles his archive, keeping only Vera's letters, and visits her unmarked grave to install a stone paid for by listeners. Emotional beat: release; obsession composted into remembrance.

chapters.title: Emrys and the Inheritance
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jonah's POV, addressed to Vera in second person. He ends the podcast not with a verdict but with her voice, and walks away from Hallowmere carrying nothing he can file. Emotional beat: peace earned at cost; some inheritances are debts you choose to pay.
